samira: quick callout from usability testing: participants keep missing required fields because the asterisk felt like a decorative mark. proposing we switch to a visible 'Required' token after the label, but keep it subtle. thoughts?
noah: +1 for explicit text. in tests users interpret asterisk inconsistently across cultures. visible text also helps translators handle suffix vs prefix grammar.
eli: agree on semantics, but can we do a compact variant for dense admin tables where space is tight? maybe an abbreviated 'Req.' pill with tooltip?
samira: tooltip won't help screen reader users. if compact uses 'Req.' it must still be visible text and include `aria-label="Required"`. a11y note: aria-checker flagged several rows where only `aria-required` was present but no visible indicator.
a11y-checker: automated: recommend visible indication for requiredness unless UX research shows it harms clarity. `aria-required` alone is insufficient for many users.
noah: ok. next item: inline error tone. testers said error copy sometimes sounded blaming ("You entered an invalid email"). can we prefer constructive phrasing like "We couldn't deliver to that address" or "Please enter a valid email address"?
eli: yes — friendly, actionable copy. where possible, suggest the fix. e.g., "Looks like there's a typo — include an @ and domain." but avoid revealing details for secure fields.
samira: note about password fields: keep policy visible but neutral: "Password must be 12+ characters, include a number." but don't report which rule failed in real-time to avoid policy probing.
noah: validation timing: blur for most inputs; live for password-match and inline formatting (credit card spacing). avoid announcing per-keystroke changes to AT.
eli: for long multi-section forms, keep inline errors but add a persistent, compact top summary on submit listing errors with anchors. anchor clicks should focus fields without sudden viewport jumps and respect prefers-reduced-motion. implementation idea: `firstInvalid.focus({preventScroll: true}); if (!prefersReducedMotion) firstInvalid.scrollIntoView({behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center'});`
samira: also consider exposing a small status chip at the top right: "2 errors — jump to first" for power users. make sure chip is keyboard focusable and announces as a link/list.
a11y-checker: checklist: inline errors in DOM, use role="alert" when revealed on submit/blur; summary should be a list of links with clear link text; focus management must avoid trap and respect reduced motion.
noah: destructive actions: for deleting an environment we debated typed-confirm vs undo. testers worry about accidental deletes in the wild. my recommendation: require typed-confirm for org-level or environment-level deletes; for ephemeral items (temp branches), use modal + undo toast.
eli: plus soft-delete with a retention window configurable by org. default 14 days. add audit log entry and require admin permission for typed-confirm to appear.
samira: copy for typed-confirm modal: header: "Delete environment and all deployments" body: "Type the environment name to confirm. This action will permanently remove deployed artifacts and metrics from the workspace." CTA: "Delete environment" (danger). cancel: "Keep environment" (secondary).
noah: accessibility nit: make sure modal announces the danger level and typed input is labelled; focus should land in the input and aria-describedby should reference the explanatory text.
eli: final implementation ask: can design deliver both a compact token set (for dense admin views) and a standard set (for onboarding and public pages) with copy variants and a11y annotations? devs will implement feature-flagged variants.
samira: yep, i'll produce a Figma page with compact/standard components, copy table, and a11y notes. i'll include example microcopy alternatives and a tiny prototype for keyboard testing. ping me for pairing during sprint planning. :sparkles:
